section_summary.extract_value: This section details logistic regression analyses examining the effects of overall Executive Function (EF) and its components (Updating, Shifting, Inhibition) on the likelihood of being in IT versus artistic professional occupations. The analyses, which appear to be from a single study (Study X), found that higher overall EF and better Shifting ability were associated with an increased likelihood of being in artistic professions, even when controlling for general cognitive ability, education, age, and gender. General cognitive ability, measured by ICAR, was not significantly associated with either profession.

section_summary.extract_value: This section details logistic regression analyses aimed at predicting involvement in artistic versus IT professional domains based on executive functions (EFs). The analyses explore the effects of overall EF and specific EFs (Updating, Shifting, Inhibition), both with and without controlling for general cognitive ability (ICAR), education, age, and gender. General cognitive ability (ICAR) was found not to be associated with either profession, while Shifting ability was consistently associated with an increased likelihood of being in artistic professions. The results are summarized in Table 6.
